title: 8 top AI-powered contact center platforms in 2026
summary: Find the right AI contact center platform. We compare top tools on agent assist, real-time transcription, pricing, and conversation orchestration.
body_text: Time to read: July 07, 2026 Written by Jesse Sumrak Twilion AI contact center technology moves fast. This article was researched and published in July 2026. Features, pricing, and product availability may have changed since publication. The contact center isn’t just a cost center to minimize. Now, thanks to AI, it's become a competitive battleground. All that’s left is to narrow down your options and find the right AI-powered contact center solution for your business. But that’s easier said than done. Some platforms are purpose-built CCaaS suites with AI bolted on. Others are developer-first infrastructure tools for teams who want to build their own. And a few (like Twilio) are doing something different: building the connective layer that lets AI agents, human agents, and customer data work as one system. Below, we’ll walk through top AI contact center platforms in 2026 to help you find the right fit for your use case. Key takeaways Agent assist could become standard: Every major platform offers some form of real-time guidance during live calls. This includes whisper coaching, suggested replies, and automated post-call summaries pushed to CRMs. Orchestration is a powerful differentiator: The platforms that win in enterprise deployments are those that can route intelligently between AI agents, human agents, and external systems without losing context in the handoff. Pricing varies wildly: From usage-based models to per-seat subscriptions to outcome-based enterprise contracts, the right choice depends heavily on your scale and build vs. buy preference. What is an AI-powered contact center platform? An AI-powered contact center platform combines the routing and channel management of a traditional contact center with AI capabilities layered across the entire conversation lifecycle. That means: Virtual agents that handle inbound volume autonomously, real-time transcription Agent assist tools that surface answers and suggested replies mid-call Automated summaries that populate your CRM without anyone typing a note Orchestration engines that route conversations between bots, human agents, and backend systems based on intent and context The top platforms are built so AI and humans share context, operate from the same conversation record, and hand off without the customer ever having to repeat themselves. What to look for in an AI contact center platform Not every platform does all of this well. Before you commit to a tool, know what matters for your use case: Real-time agent assist: Does the platform surface answers and coaching during live calls, or only after? CRM and help desk integration: Will post-call summaries and transcripts automatically push to Salesforce, Zendesk, ServiceNow, or your system of record? Multi-agent orchestration: Can the platform route between multiple AI agents , escalate to a human in under 10 seconds, and pass full context when it does? Tool calling and API access: Can your AI agent take action (update a ticket, check an order, modify a subscription), or is it limited to answering questions? Guardrails and governance: Does the platform give you control over what the AI can and can't do before it goes live with real customers? Cross-channel context sharing: Can the platform carry what it learned in a chat conversation into the follow-up voice call? Twilio Conversation Memory and Conversation Orchestrator build a persistent customer profile that every agent and AI system can access regardless of which channel the customer used last. Knowledge grounding and retrieval: Does the platform connect directly to your FAQs , docs, and policies to index them as "source of truth" data for fast, verified answers? Pricing model fit: Usage-based pricing rewards efficiency at scale, while per-seat models are more predictable. 8 top AI-powered contact center platforms in 2026 Twilio Most contact center platforms were built for chatbots. Twilio is built for what comes next: autonomous AI agents that act on behalf of your business, work alongside human agents, and never make a customer start over. The model is composable by design. You bring your own LLMs, AI agents, and data, then connect everything into a single conversation layer that carries context across every channel, every handoff, and every interaction. Key features: Conversation Relay : Low-latency voice AI with bring-your-own-LLM and HIPAA-eligible infrastructure Conversation Intelligence : Real-time transcription, sentiment analysis, and CRM-ready auto summaries Conversation Orchestrator : Multi-agent routing with context-rich AI-to-human handoffs Conversation Memory : Persistent customer profiles with semantic recall across every channel Agent Connect : Connect any AI agent to Twilio Voice and Messaging For: Builders and CX teams who want to design their own AI agent architecture on a flexible, API-first platform. NICE CXone NICE CXone is an established enterprise CCaaS platform. Its Enlighten AI suite covers the full interaction lifecycle: virtual agents for self-service, Copilot for Agents for real-time whisper coaching and suggested replies, Real-Time Interaction Guidance for in-call prompts, AutoSummary for CRM-ready post-call notes, and analytics that evaluate interactions. Key features: Copilot for Agents: Real-time suggested replies and knowledge surfacing during live calls Real-Time Interaction Guidance: Whisper coaching prompts delivered at the exact moment they matter Enlighten AI: Analyzes interactions for sentiment, compliance, and coaching opportunities AutoSummary: Post-call summaries auto-generated and pushed to connected CRM systems Agent Assist Hub: Low-code integration for Google CCAI, Salesforce Assist, and more For: Large enterprises that want a proven, all-in-one CCaaS suite with mature AI capabilities and strong compliance coverage. Sierra Sierra is a high-profile AI agent platform. Its agents go beyond answering questions to take real action in backend systems. Pricing is outcome-based. Key features: Autonomous resolution: AI agents process returns, update subscriptions, and call backend APIs Agent OS: Core platform for building, deploying, and governing agents across all channels Sierra Speaks: Voice AI with context-aware human handoff and AI-generated summaries Ghostwriter: Build production-ready agents from SOPs, transcripts, or plain English prompts Observability: Full visibility into tool calls, knowledge lookups, latency, and agent decisions For: Enterprise brands with large contact center volumes and the budget for an outcome-based engagement model. AWS Amazon Connect Amazon Connect is AWS's cloud-native contact center service. It’s usage-based, deeply integrated with the AWS ecosystem, and increasingly built around generative AI via Bedrock. It works for teams already on AWS who want contact center AI that plugs into existing data infrastructure without additional middleware. Key features: Connect Wisdom: Real-time AI-powered recommendations surfaced to agents during live calls Contact Lens: Real-time transcription, sentiment analysis, and automated call summaries Amazon Lex: Conversational AI and natural language IVR for customer self-service Bedrock integration: Generative AI layer for virtual agents and conversation summarization Usage-based pricing: Pay per contact minute For: Teams building on AWS who want contact center AI that integrates natively with existing cloud infrastructure and data pipelines. Vonage Vonage (now part of Ericsson) brings a CPaaS heritage to the contact center, offering virtual agents, real-time transcription, sentiment analysis, and a visual AI Studio. A solid fit for mid-market teams that want communications APIs and contact center AI from a single vendor without the complexity of enterprise CCaaS. Key features: Vonage AI Studio: Drag-and-drop builder for AI conversation flows across voice and chat Real-time transcription: Live call-to-text with sentiment scoring during active interactions Virtual agents: Automated self-service across inbound voice and digital channels CRM integrations: Pre-built connectors for Salesforce, Dynamics, Zendesk, and HubSpot CPaaS foundation: Voice, SMS, and messaging APIs alongside contact center tooling For: Mid-market businesses looking for combined CPaaS and contact center AI capabilities without the complexity of enterprise CCaaS platforms. Sinch Sinch is a global communications platform that has expanded CPaaS roots into AI-powered customer engagement. Virtual agents, real-time coaching, and conversation analytics sit alongside voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and email APIs. Its infrastructure helps companies serving customers across multiple regions at scale. Key features: Virtual agents: AI-powered self-service across voice and digital with human escalation Real-time AI insights: Sentiment analysis and conversation signals during live interactions Omnichannel reach: Voice, SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, email, and in-app messaging Global infrastructure: Carrier-grade delivery with local number support Developer APIs: Programmable building blocks for custom contact center applications For: Global businesses that need omnichannel customer engagement with AI features layered on proven CPaaS infrastructure. Infobip Infobip is an omnichannel customer engagement platform with a contact center product (Conversations) and AI chatbot builder (Answers) that cover self-service, live agent handling, and AI-assisted interactions. It provides WhatsApp, SMS, RCS, email, voice, and social messaging all in one platform, with minimal infrastructure overhead. Key features: Answers: No-code chatbot builder with NLP, intent recognition, and multi-channel deployment Conversations: Unified agent inbox with AI assist, routing, and omnichannel management People CDP: Customer data platform powering AI personalization and conversation context Channel breadth: WhatsApp, RCS, SMS, email, voice, and live chat Reporting: Real-time and historical analytics across channels with CSAT tracking For: Businesses that need AI-powered customer engagement across a wide range of messaging channels with minimal custom development. Bandwidth Bandwidth is an API-first communications platform known for enterprise voice infrastructure that has expanded into AI-powered voice experiences. Its direct carrier access helps teams that need control over call quality, latency, and number management while layering AI on top of their own contact center stack. Key features: Enterprise voice APIs: Direct carrier access with global PSTN connectivity at scale AI voice integrations: Native connections with leading STT, TTS, and LLM providers Real-time transcription: Low-latency call-to-text for live agent assist and analytics workflows Call summaries: Automated post-call summaries for CRM or help desk delivery Reliability SLAs: Carrier-grade infrastructure with enterprise uptime guarantees For: Enterprises building custom AI voice applications that need carrier-grade reliability and direct control over voice infrastructure. The future of AI contact centers The shift happening in contact centers right now is bigger than adding AI features to an existing stack. We’re now thinking about how to enable AI and humans to share context, memory, and conversation history across channels. This requires orchestration engines that can route intelligently and hand off cleanly. And it requires the flexibility to bring your own models, your own data, and your own preferred tools—without being locked into one vendor's ecosystem. The platforms that get that right are the ones worth building on. Get started with Twilio Twilio's Conversational AI gives your team the building blocks to connect AI agents and human agents across every channel with the context to act on what they know. No walled garden or forced swap of your existing stack. Start for free or chat with sales to talk through your use case. Frequently asked questions Which contact center software lets an AI agent monitor a live call and whisper suggested replies to a human agent? Twilio's Conversation Intelligence surfaces real-time signals and coaching cues during voice interactions when combined with Twilio Flex. NICE CXone delivers this through Real-Time Interaction Guidance (RTIG) and Copilot for Agents. AWS Connect Wisdom also surfaces AI recommendations during live calls. Which contact center platforms have built-in agent assist and workflow automation? Twilio combines Conversation Intelligence for real-time transcription, sentiment analysis, and in-call coaching signals with Conversation Orchestrator for rules-based workflow automation and routing—all surfaced inside Twilio Flex for human agents. It's one of the few platforms where agent assist and orchestration share a unified conversation layer rather than operating as separate products. What services provide real-time call transcription plus auto summaries pushed into major CRMs and help desks? Twilio Conversation Intelligence analyzes voice and messaging conversations and can push summaries and insights to downstream systems. NICE CXone AutoSummary generates post-call summaries that automatically populate supported CRM applications. AWS Contact Lens provides real-time transcription and call summaries that can route into AWS data pipelines and connected systems. How do pricing models for conversational AI platforms compare? Twilio uses usage-based pricing so you pay for what you use across Conversation Relay, Conversation Intelligence, Conversation Orchestrator, and other products, with no per-seat minimums. That model rewards efficiency at scale and makes it easier to start small and grow. AWS Amazon Connect is similarly usage-based. NICE CXone is quote-based with per-feature licensing. Which platforms can route requests between multiple AI agents and fall back to a human in under 10 seconds? Twilio Conversation Orchestrator is purpose-built for this: it routes conversations across channels and AI agents using configurable rules, and passes full conversation context to human agents on handoff. NICE CXone coordinates AI agents and human escalation within its unified platform. What's the top platform for building an AI support agent that can call APIs and update tickets? For developer teams building custom AI agents, Twilio Agent Connect lets you connect any AI agent (OpenAI, Bedrock, LangChain) directly to Twilio voice and messaging channels, with the AI agent handling tool calls and API interactions in your own runtime. Sierra is an out-of-the-box option for action-taking AI agents that connect to backend systems via its Agent Data Platform. Which platforms sync AI agent memory with a CRM in real time? Twilio Conversation Memory builds persistent customer profiles from every interaction and syncs directly with Salesforce, Segment, and Snowflake.AWS Amazon Connect can route post-interaction data into connected AWS systems, though real-time sync requires additional configuration. What tools support real-time handoff to a human agent with full conversation history? Twilio Conversation Orchestrator passes the full context on every escalation so agents never start cold. That context includes everything Conversation Memory has captured across all prior interactions, not just the current conversation. Which conversational AI and agentic orchestration platforms have the best integrations? Twilio integrates across voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and RCS, connects any LLM through Agent Connect, and pushes summaries to Salesforce, Zendesk, and ServiceNow. Which vendors offer prebuilt connectors for AI agents to integrate with Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Zendesk? Twilio pushes AI-generated summaries and transcripts to Salesforce, Zendesk, and ServiceNow, and Conversation Memory syncs profiles directly with Salesforce.

title: Research Solutions Wins EPIC 2025 Gold Award For Innovation
summary: The EPIC 2025 Gold Award acknowledges Research Solutions' impact in revolutionizing how researchers discover, validate, and cite scientific work.
body_text: The Award, Presented At The SSP EPIC Awards Ceremony, Acknowledges Research Solutions' Impact In Revolutionizing How Researchers Discover, Validate, & Cite Scientific Work HENDERSON, Nev., Jul. 29, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Research Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: RSSS), a leading provider of AI-powered scientific research tools, announces that Scite's Smart Citations technology has been recognized with the 2025 Gold Award for Excellence in Publishing by the Society for Scholarly Publishing (SSP) in the Hosting Platforms Feature category. The prestigious award from the scholarly publishing industry's premier conference highlights Scite's transformative role in addressing the research reproducibility crisis and making peer-reviewed research more accessible across industries and institutions. The recognition underscores Research Solutions' unique approach to building Smart Citations technology through strategic partnerships with dozens of leading publishers. These direct indexing agreements enable comprehensive coverage across disciplines, providing researchers with intelligent tools to assess the reliability and context of cited research regardless of institutional affiliation or funding limitations. By partnering directly with publishers, Research Solutions ensures that Smart Citations technology delivers the most complete and accurate citation analysis available in the market. Built on Research Solutions' extensive publisher partnerships, Smart Citations deliver contextual information about how research has been cited—whether findings have been supported, contradicted, or merely mentioned. This comprehensive publisher coverage enables researchers to make more informed decisions about the reliability of scientific claims. Research Solutions' publisher partnership model provides access to millions of full-text articles through indexing agreements with leading publishers alongside Open Access content, ensuring comprehensive coverage that competitors cannot match. This robust dataset, further enriched with author, affiliation, and topic metadata from CrossRef, DataCite, and OpenAlex, enables Smart Citations' intelligent algorithms to analyze citation networks and identify trending research, emerging controversies, and consensus-building studies. Detailed citation analysis helps combat common challenges in scholarly publishing, including citation manipulation, superficial referencing, and the propagation of unreliable research findings. The technology also provides researchers with a more nuanced understanding of the research landscape than traditional citation metrics alone. This capability is essential as the volume of published research continues to grow, making it increasingly difficult for researchers to stay current with developments in their fields. SSP's EPIC Award recognition validates Research Solutions' broader mission to enhance the quality and accessibility of scientific research through innovative technology and strategic publisher partnerships. Smart Citations are part of the company's comprehensive suite of research tools designed to support evidence-based decision-making across academic, industry, and policy contexts. The recognition reflects the scholarly publishing community's growing acknowledgment of the need for more sophisticated tools to navigate the complex research ecosystem. As concerns about research quality and reproducibility continue to mount, solutions such as Smart Citations represent essential infrastructure for maintaining public trust in scientific research while supporting the broader goals of open science and evidence-based practice across sectors. Publishers and researchers can review journal-specific coverage details at https://scite.ai/journals . About Research Solutions Research Solutions (NASDAQ: RSSS) is a vertical SaaS and AI company that simplifies research workflow for academic institutions, life science companies, and research organizations worldwide. As one of the only publisher-independent marketplaces for scientific, technical, and medical (STM) content, the company uniquely combines AI-powered tools—including an intelligent research assistant and full-text search capabilities—with seamless access to both open access and paywalled research. The platform enables organizations to discover, access, manage and analyze scientific literature more efficiently, accelerating the pace of scientific discovery. For more information about Research Solutions, visit: www.researchsolutions.com | LinkedIn | Facebook | X SOURCE Research Solutions, Inc. Media inquiries can be directed to Lydia Lindenberg, Director of Content Marketing, llindenberg@researchsolutions.com .

title: Small Businesses Need Telcos for Cybersecurity
body_text: Table of Contents The New Reality: High Awareness, Low Preparedness Complexity Is the Real Threat Multiplier A Shift in Who SMBs Trust Willingness to Pay Exists, With the Right Conditions Cybersecurity Moves Into the Network The Bottom Line Next Steps Small businesses have quietly become one of the most important battlegrounds in cybersecurity. As digital tools, from cloud apps to mobile-first workflows, have leveled the playing field, they have also expanded the attack surface. The result is a fundamental shift: SMBs are now operating at enterprise-like speed and scale, but without enterprise-level protection. This gap between exposure and readiness is the most important takeaway from the latest findings in the Small Businesses, Big Cyber Targets report based on a recent study conducted by Allot and Dynata, where we surveyed small business owners from around the world to get their impressions about cybersecurity and telcos. And it carries major implications for both SMBs and for the telecom providers that serve them. The New Reality: High Awareness, Low Preparedness One of the most striking findings is what can best be described as a “preparedness paradox.” SMBs are increasingly aware of cyber risks, yet remain structurally underprepared to address them. The data makes this clear: Nearly 1 in 3 SMBs have already experienced a cyber incident tied to their business 95% use personal devices for work, dramatically expanding the attack surface Yet adoption of protection mechanisms remains low This isn’t due to complacency. It reflects a deeper structural issue: SMBs lack the time, expertise, and resources to deploy and manage complex security stacks. In other words, the problem isn’t awareness. It’s usability. Complexity Is the Real Threat Multiplier The survey highlights that cybersecurity complexity has become a barrier in itself. SMBs are not rejecting security; they are overwhelmed by it. Decision-makers consistently prioritize: Efficacy and protection (59%) Total cost of ownership (47%) Ease of use and management (41%) This reinforces a key shift in how cybersecurity is evaluated. SMBs are no longer buying features. They are buying outcomes. They want protection that works, that fits their budget and that doesn’t require ongoing management. This aligns directly with Allot’s messaging principle of “innovative accessibility”, making complex security simple and usable without requiring specialized expertise. A Shift in Who SMBs Trust Perhaps the most important, and most disruptive, insight is who SMBs now see as their cybersecurity partner. Across markets, 63% of SMBs say they would trust their telecom provider to deliver cybersecurity. This reflects a deeper behavioral shift. SMBs already rely on telecom providers for connectivity, the backbone of their business. Cybersecurity is increasingly seen as a natural extension of that relationship. Trust, simplicity, and embedded delivery matter more than traditional vendor positioning. For telecom operators, this is not just validation. It is a strategic opening. Willingness to Pay Exists, With the Right Conditions Another long-standing assumption challenged by the data is that SMBs are unwilling to pay for cybersecurity. In reality, 84% say they are willing to pay their telecom provider for cybersecurity services. But the conditions are clear: Pricing must be predictable and transparent Deployment must be simple and frictionless The service must require little to no ongoing management SMBs want cybersecurity to behave like connectivity: always on, fully integrated, and effortless. This is exactly where network-based, zero-touch security models become not just relevant, but necessary. Cybersecurity Moves Into the Network Taken together, these findings point to a structural shift in how cybersecurity will be delivered to SMBs. Traditional models – complex tools, multiple vendors, endpoint-heavy solutions – are poorly aligned with SMB reality. The winners in this space will be those who deliver protection differently: Embedded within the network Delivered through existing relationships Designed for simplicity and scale This aligns directly with Allot’s positioning as a network intelligence-led cybersecurity provider, delivering zero-touch protection at scale through telecom partners. The opportunity is not to replicate enterprise security. It is to redefine cybersecurity for the masses: accessible, automated, and invisible to the user. The Bottom Line SMBs are no longer a secondary market in cybersecurity. They are the center of gravity and they are underserved. The gap between rising threats and limited resources is growing. But so is the opportunity to close it. Telecom providers are uniquely positioned to do exactly that. Next Steps The full picture and the detailed data behind these insights is available in the complete report, titled Small Businesses, Big Cyber Targets . Read the report now to explore the findings and uncover where the next opportunities in SMB cybersecurity will emerge. You can also view the on-demand webinar in which we discuss the SMB cybersecurity survey in detail and hear from Wes Hamrick from Verizon who talks about the challenges and solutions related to offering cybersecurity services to SMBs.

body_text: Sezzle Named a World’s Top Fintech Company, Best Online Platform, and Top Employer for 2026 July 22, 2026 Minneapolis, MN, July 22, 2026 ( GLOBE NEWSWIRE ) -- Sezzle Inc. (NASDAQ: SEZL ) ( Sezzle or Company ) has earned recognition from three of the industry's leading publications — CNBC, Newsweek, and U.S. News & World Report — for its leadership across fintech, platform quality, and workplace culture. The honors come as Sezzle raised its FY2026 financial guidance alongside its first quarter results , underscoring the Company's continued momentum in scaling its all-in-one financial platform and its mission to financially empower the next generation. CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies 2026 Sezzle has been named to CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies 2026 in the 'Payments' category, presented by CNBC and Statista Inc. The list recognizes top fintech companies across categories, including Payments, Neobanking, Alternative Financing, Wealth Technology, Digital Assets, Enterprise Fintech, Insurtech, and Regtech. The data used in the analysis was derived from extensive research conducted by Statista, evaluating company performance, industry impact, and market presence. Newsweek’s America’s Best Online Platforms 2026 Sezzle has also been awarded on Newsweek’s America’s Best Online Platforms 2026 list , presented by Newsweek and Statista Inc. The ranking awards the top 500 platforms that set the standard for quality and trust across four evaluation dimensions: Nationwide Online Survey: Representative online survey of over 15,000 online-service users, including subjective criteria such as layout evaluation and purchase probability. Traffic Growth: Analysis of traffic growth (number of website visitors) of online platforms. Technical Performance: Analysis of various technical metrics including usage duration and bounce rate. Apps & Mobile Usability: Evaluation of the mobile experience based on app availability, user ratings, and mobile-optimized display. U.S. News & World Report Best Company to Work For Sezzle has been named a U.S. News & World Report 2026–2027 Best Company to Work For . title: How long before we stop reading the code?
summary: Don't kill the code reviews; just move the human checkpoint upstream to reviewing intent, specs, plans, constraints, and acceptance criteria. Code is actually the least important part of the reviews.
body_text: Code review has become the bottleneck. AI generates code faster than any human can read it, and asking another AI to do the reading doesn’t solve the underlying problem. The way out is to move the human checkpoint upstream, to the point where intent is defined, before any code is written. The review bottleneck Code review as a quality gate was already showing cracks even before AI coding tools. Microsoft research analyzed 1.5 million review comments across five major projects and found that as change size grows, the share of useful comments shrinks. Not fewer comments, less useful ones. We already stopped reading code for the most part. Then AI coding tools arrived and broke the model entirely. Teams with high AI adoption are now merging 98% more PRs, while review times have climbed 91% . We’ve all experienced how unreliable agents writing code can be, and no one wants to ship AI slop into production, so engineering teams keep telling themselves, “We caught AI doing dumb things once, so we must always check it.” They tell themselves that code review is the quality gate, but in reality, either PRs sit for days or engineers skim 500-line diffs and rubber-stamp approvals. AI code review is still a code review There is no way we’re outreading the machines. And when humans can’t keep up, the instinct is to use AI to review AI-generated code . Teams are already doing this with Cursor rules files, AGENTS.md configurations, and dedicated AI review tools. A senior engineer codifies years of review standards into a rules file. Engineers are creating their own AI-powered skill to review the code. Sometimes they also use famous personalities, asking AI to review code like Linus Torvalds or Kent Beck! The LLM reads incoming PRs against it. Developers skim the output and merge. This approach inherits three failure modes that no amount of prompt tuning will solve. The first is non-determinism: the same code can produce different reviews in multiple runs. That is not a quality gate. The second is missing intent: the LLM reads a diff in isolation, pattern-matching against its training data without understanding what the code was supposed to do. The third is duplicate blind spots: when the same model writes the code and reviews the code, it misses the same things both times. You have not added a check. You have added a mirror. Teams that built these rules files did the right thing. They articulated what they cared about. The mistake was dropping those standards into a system that cannot reliably enforce them. Three conditions have to be met for a team to get off the PR-review treadmill without losing quality. Each is a maturity step, and each needs to be in place before the next one delivers real value. 1. Codify code review feedback into deterministic checks There are two types of code review comments: something about coding standards, organizational standards, or expectations; and behavior/judgment-based comments – how a particular logic should function. The first one should be a guardrail that can be checked through AST. Behavior can also be verified through execution tests; however, we should still review this during the human checkpoint. Most standards that teams enforce repeatedly; things like “every new endpoint must have tracing spans” or “error paths must emit metrics” or “auth failures must be logged with structured fields,” are either statically checkable through AST analysis or verifiable through execution tests. A rule like “new endpoints must have OTel spans” becomes an AST check on route handler decorators. “Error paths emit metrics” becomes an execution test: hit the endpoint with bad input and assert that the counter increments. When teams actually pull their last 100 PR review comments and sort them into three buckets (deterministic, execution-testable, genuine judgment), you might end with a split around 45/30/25. Three-quarters of review feedback may be codifiable. The work to codify it is real, but it is finite. Once a check is written, it never needs a reviewer again. This is where we can and should leverage AI and beat AI slop with AI. 2. Move the human checkpoint upstream I’m not saying we should ‘dangerously skip reading code’ and stop reviewing AI-written code. The reviewer isn’t absent here; they’re more present than ever, just earlier. Instead of reviewing a 400-line diff after the code exists, the reviewer reads an 8-line on intentpec before it does: acceptance criteria, non-goals, blast radius. The reviewer’s job shifts from “Does this look right?” to “Are we solving the right problem with the right constraints?” which is closer to an RFC review than a line-by-line code review. This is also where the knowledge-sharing function of review survives. When AI writes code, intent exists in a prompt that was never saved, a ticket that doesn’t capture the decision-making, or only in the engineer’s head. The implementation gets preserved. The reasoning behind it does not. Reviewing specs in the intent-driven verification process changes that. Reviewers reading acceptance criteria are reading the decisions behind the implementation, not the implementation itself. The decisions that matter, the ones currently lost in prompt conversations with agents, become the reviewable artifact. In practice, this does not require a formal methodology. A Jira ticket with a few sentences on scope, a short list of acceptance criteria, and a note on what is out of scope can serve as the spec. The format matters less than the discipline of defining intent before generating code. 3. Use LLMs where deterministic can’t reach Some review feedback is genuine judgment: pattern recognition over context or questioning an architectural choice. This is where LLMs earn their place, not as the primary check but as a scoped fallback. The wrong approach is one where an LLM reads a diff and produces free-form opinions. The right approach is a separate verifier agent with no shared context with the implementing agent, a scoped prompt, and structured output with file references and reasoning for each finding. Let the verifier agent capture evidence using a deterministic methodology (screenshots, API responses, server logs) to reduce the likelihood of hallucinations. Replace code reviews with verifying intent This is the system we are building at Aviator. Verify accelerates code reviews with verified intent. Specs are written collaboratively with AI, reviewed and approved by humans, implemented with whatever coding tool the team prefers (Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, or manual), then verified deterministically against each acceptance criterion. Before submitting the change, your coding agent reviews the discussion and submits the intent and behavior details to Aviator. These get reviewed and approved by humans. The difference from AI code review is fundamental. The same code always produces the same verification result. The system checks against declared intent rather than whatever the model notices on a given run. Verification becomes a matter of checking the output against agreed-upon criteria , not of trying to reverse-engineer intent from the implementation. How long would it take for your team? Here’s the homework for you. Pull your team’s last 1,000 PR review comments; it should take no more than a couple of hours. Sort each one, asking, is this deterministic, is this execution-testable, or is this genuine judgment? The first two are your guardrail backlog, concrete, finite, and prioritizable. The third is what’s left for humans (and LLMs). From there, review the behavior, the intent, and the decision made while making the changes. These are the decisions the author makes while providing feedback to the agent in a terminal or IDE. Then review the evidence Don’t kill the code reviews; “code” is actually the least important part of the reviews. This article was originally published on The New Stack .
